intro: The most common reason homeowners in Borthwickpark look into wet room installation is accessibility — either planning ahead for older age, adapting a bathroom for a family member with mobility needs, or simply wanting a more practical, open showering space that works better with the layout of an older property. Wet rooms have become one of the most sought-after bathroom upgrades in Midlothian, and in a small, characterful community like Borthwickpark, the investment tends to add genuine long-term value to the home. Whether you're working with a compact cottage bathroom or a larger space in a more modern property, a properly installed wet room transforms daily life in a way that a standard shower enclosure simply can't match.
localContext: Borthwickpark sits in a part of Midlothian where the housing stock is genuinely varied — you have older stone-built properties and period cottages that were never designed with modern wet rooms in mind, alongside more recently built homes on modern estates where the groundwork is considerably more straightforward. That distinction matters a lot when planning a wet room. In older stone-built properties in Borthwickpark, walls can be uneven, floor joists may need reinforcing to take the tanking membrane and tile weight, and there's sometimes less depth beneath floorboards to accommodate a linear drain. These aren't reasons to avoid a wet room — they're just reasons to use a tradesperson who understands the local building stock. Borthwickpark is also in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale buildup on screens, drains, and fittings is a real consideration. Opting for larger format tiles with fewer grout lines, and choosing quality chrome or brushed brass fittings with better scale resistance, will save you maintenance headaches down the line.
serviceDetail: A full wet room installation in Borthwickpark typically follows a clear sequence of work, and understanding it helps you manage expectations around timescales and disruption. The job begins with a thorough survey of the existing bathroom — the installer needs to assess the floor construction, drainage options, wall substrate condition, and whether any structural work is needed before the waterproofing stage begins. In period cottages or older stone-built homes in Borthwickpark, this survey stage is especially important and shouldn't be rushed. Once the scope is confirmed, the existing bathroom is stripped back to bare walls and floor. The most critical phase is the tanking — applying a fully waterproof membrane across the floor and up the walls to a suitable height. This has to be done correctly; poor tanking is the single biggest cause of wet room failures and water damage. After tanking, the floor is built up with a screed that incorporates the required fall toward the drain — typically a gradient of around 1:80. Tiling then follows, with wall tiles going up before floor tiles come down. Finally, the sanitaryware, shower valve, screen (if required), and all fittings are installed and tested. A straightforward installation in a standard-sized bathroom usually takes five to seven working days, though older properties in Borthwickpark may add a couple of days depending on what's uncovered during the strip-out.
pricing: In Borthwickpark, a realistic budget for a full wet room installation runs from around £6,000 to £12,000, depending on the size of the space, the complexity of the existing structure, and the specification of materials you choose. A mid-range wet room in a modern estate property, with quality tiles and a decent shower valve, tends to sit between £6,500 and £8,500. In older stone-built properties or period cottages, structural prep and floor reinforcement can push costs toward £9,000 to £12,000. Choosing premium fittings, underfloor heating, or bespoke tiling layouts will also move the price upward. Always get a fixed-price quote that covers labour, materials, and any contingency work uncovered during strip-out.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickpark and the wider Midlothian area genuinely matters for a job like this. Local installers will have worked in the older stone-built properties and period cottages that are common here — they won't be surprised by uneven walls, shallow floor voids, or original lime plaster that needs careful handling. They're also more likely to have established relationships with local building merchants, which can keep material costs and lead times sensible. Practically speaking, a local wet room specialist can visit Borthwickpark quickly for a survey, is easier to reach if a question comes up mid-job, and has a local reputation to protect.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwickpark?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than in a modern property. Stone walls and older timber floors need careful assessment before tanking begins. A good installer will check floor joist depth, wall condition, and drainage options before quoting. It's more involved, but period cottages in Borthwickpark can have excellent wet rooms with the right approach.

faqs.q: How do I deal with limescale on my new wet room in a hard water area like Borthwickpark?
faqs.a: Borthwickpark's moderately hard water does mean limescale is a consideration. Specifying large-format tiles with minimal grout lines reduces surface area for scale to cling to. A quality squeegee after each use makes a real difference. Some homeowners also fit an inline water softener or scale inhibitor on the shower supply, which protects fittings and keeps the drain running cleanly long-term.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwickpark?
faqs.a: For a standard bathroom conversion in a modern Borthwickpark property, expect five to seven working days. In older stone-built homes or period cottages where structural prep is needed, allow seven to ten days. Your installer should give you a clear programme before work starts, including any contingency time for surprises uncovered during the strip-out phase.

faqs.q: Is a wet room a good investment for a property in Borthwickpark?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. A well-executed wet room adds practical value and is increasingly expected by buyers in this part of Midlothian, particularly in higher-value properties. Accessibility features also broaden appeal significantly. The key is using a properly qualified installer — a poorly waterproofed wet room can cause serious structural damage, so quality of workmanship matters far more than saving a few hundred pounds upfront.
